lines.text: Watching football this Thanksgiving? That yellow first down line isn't painted on the field. So how does it stay glued to the grass?
Each camera is fitted with sensors that track every pan, tilt, zoom and focus change.
Engineers also map the field into a 3D model, even its slight curve.
Combine the two, and a computer knows exactly where that yard line should appear in the shot, recalculating thirty times a second.
Then the trick: the line is only drawn over grass colored pixels, so players seem to walk right over it.
The video is delayed by a few frames so the line and picture stay perfectly in sync.
It debuted on ESPN in the late nineteen nineties, and now it's hard to imagine football without it.
